record_type_quote: Starting with the papers citing a seminal publication in the field, we conducted replications of 20 studies that evaluate the role of scarcity priming in pain sensitivity, resource allocation, materialism, and many other domains.

targets.authors: Abeyta, A. A.; Routledge, C.; Kersten, M.; Cox, C. R.
targets.title: The existential cost of economic insecurity: Threatened financial security undercuts meaning.
targets.evidence_quote: Study 2 from:
targets.outcome_quote: Though this study did not replicate the original, both studies resulted in effects in the same direction such that MLQ was higher in the control condition than the economic scarcity condition.

targets.authors: Bickel, W. K.; Wilson, A. G.; Chen, C.; Koffarnus, M. N.; Franck, C. T.
targets.title: Stuck in time: Negative income shock constricts the temporal window of valuation spanning the future and the past
targets.evidence_quote: Bickel et al., 2016 Replication
targets.outcome_quote: Although most of our replications did not approach statistical significance, those that did (4, 16–18) shared some common features.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The main text identifies references 4 and 16–18 as its four successful replications; Bickel is reference 16. Reduced effect size does not override that verdict.

targets.authors: Camerer, C. F.; et al.
targets.title: Evaluating the replicability of social science experiments in Nature and Science between 2010 and 2015
targets.evidence_quote: Camerer et al. (2018) replication of study 1 from “Some Consequences of Having Too Little” by Shah, Mullainathan, and Shafir (2012)
targets.outcome_reasoning: Closest named target in the chain is Camerer et al. (2018). The project report explicitly judges failure against Shah (2012), but gives no unambiguous substantive outcome comparison against Camerer. The spreadsheet has original F(1,617)=0.1389 and the replication is nonsignificant, which suggests agreement with a null, but the supplied narrative does not settle that target verdict.

targets.authors: Chou, E. Y.; Parmar, B. L.; Galinsky, A. D.
targets.title: Economic insecurity increases physical pain
targets.evidence_quote: Chou et al. (2016), Study 3
targets.outcome_quote: Although most of our replications did not approach statistical significance, those that did (4, 16–18) shared some common features.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Reference 4 belongs to the explicitly named set of four successes.

targets.authors: Cook, L. A.; Sadeghein, R.
targets.title: Effects of perceived scarcity on financial decision making
targets.evidence_quote: Cook & Sadeghein (2018), Study 3
targets.outcome_quote: Although most of our replications did not approach statistical significance, those that did (4, 16–18) shared some common features.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Reference 17 belongs to the named successful set. The original central interaction was not significant but the replication was; author verdict governs.

targets.authors: Durante, K. M.; Griskevicius, V.; Redden, J. P.; White, A. E.
targets.title: Spending on Daughters versus Sons in Economic Recessions.
targets.evidence_quote: Replication of Durante et. al (2015), Spending on daughters versus sons in economic recessions
targets.outcome_quote: While the replication did also find a significant interaction, it was not in the same direction and the original effect size was not included in the replication 95% confidence interval.

targets.authors: Emery; Walsh; Slotter
targets.evidence_quote: Emery et al., 2015; Study 3
targets.outcome_quote: In the replication, this ANCOVA revealed a non-significant effect of condition on self-ratings of the target attribute participants generated at the beginning of the study after viewing the dating profile, F(2, 438) = 1.04, p = .36, partial 𝜂2 = .005 (r = 0.071), controlling for initial self-ratings, F(1, 438) = 60.92, p < .001, partial 𝜂2 = .12 (also see Table 1).
targets.outcome_reasoning: Both primary project attempts failed the main self-expansion test and the manipulation check. No author verdict that the attempts are uninformative. Full target title and author initials are absent from the acquired project reports and main reference list.

targets.authors: Fernbach; Kan; Lynch
targets.evidence_quote: Study 2 of Fernbach, Kan, and Lynch 2015 contains two primary predictions and analyses.
targets.outcome_quote: In the replication, there was no interaction of constraint and plan type on planning mix, F(1,222) = 0.29, p = .752. In testing for response times, there was an interaction of constraint and plan time on log-transformed response time, F(2, 299) = 3.04, p = .049.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The project report compares failure of the original planning-mix finding and a significant response-time interaction. An added model matching the original fails too; no overall verdict overrides the reported partly agreeing comparisons. Full title and author initials unavailable in acquired text.

targets.authors: Kristofferson, K.; McFerran, B.; Morales, A. C.; Dahl, D. W.
targets.title: The dark side of scarcity promotions: how exposure to limited-quantity promotions can induce aggression
targets.evidence_quote:
This experiment is a direct replication of Experiment 5 in "The dark side of scarcity promotions: how exposure to limited-quantity promotions can induce
         aggression" in the Journal of Consumer Research (2016).
targets.outcome_quote: In addition, the hypothesized interaction was not significant (F(1, 385) = 0.005, p = .945, partial eta-squared = .000).
targets.outcome_reasoning: Primary write-up dates the target 2016, whereas the project summary table labels it 2017. The central scarcity-aggression interaction fails.

targets.authors: Layous, K.; Kurtz, J.; Chancellor, J.; Lyubomirsky, S.
targets.title: Reframing the ordinary: Imagining time as scarce increases well-being.
targets.evidence_quote: Layous, K., Kurtz, J., Chancellor, J., & Lyubomirsky, S. (2018). Reframing the ordinary: Imagining time as scarce increases well-being. The Journal of Positive Psychology, 13(3), 301-308.
targets.outcome_quote: We did not observe the predicted interaction between condition and week, F(2, 378.51) = 0.68, p = 0.51. That is, well-being did not change more over time for the LTM condition as opposed to the control.

targets.authors: Lee; Baumgartner; Winterich
targets.evidence_quote: Lee, Baumgartner, & Winterich, 2018, Study 4_Replication
targets.outcome_quote: Overall, the key hypothesis of attenuated interaction and the mediation mechanism were not supported by the data.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Overall verdict governs despite a supported prestige association. Full target title and author initials are absent from the acquired text.

targets.authors: Mani, A.; Mullainathan, S.; Shafir, E.; Zhao, J.
targets.title: Poverty impedes cognitive function
targets.evidence_quote: Following Study 4 from Mani, Mullainathan, Shafir, & Zhao (2013), a household income-diverse sample was recruited (Median=$55,000, min=$5000, max=over $200,000).
targets.outcome_quote: Contrary to prior results (Mani et al., 2013), there was no robust interaction between income and condition (F(1,224) = 0.17, p = .678).

targets.authors: Mehta; Zhu
targets.title: Creating When You Have Less: The Impact of Resource Scarcity on Product Use Creativity
targets.evidence_quote: Experiment 2 – Creating When You Have Less: The Impact of Resource Scarcity on Product Use Creativity, (Mehta & Zhu, 2015)
targets.outcome_quote: A chi-square test revealed no significant effect of resource availability on the correctness of the solutions (X22, N=319=2.224,  p= .329).
targets.outcome_reasoning: Preregistration states the original scarcity-enhanced creativity prediction; main test and pairwise comparisons fail. Primary project write-up labels the original 2015; summary table labels it 2016. Initials unavailable.

targets.authors: Monga; May; Bagchi
targets.evidence_quote: Monga, May, Bagchi, 2017 Study 4_Replication
targets.outcome_quote: A main effect of procedure emerged, such that the desired wage rate was higher in the TEL (vs. MEL) condition (MTEL = $15.06, SD = $9.54; MMEL = $8.71, SD = $8.21; F(1, 463) = 22.26, p < .01, Cohen’s d = 0.179). Contrary to the results of Monga, May, and Bagchi (2017), no main effect of timing emerged, such there was no significant difference of the wage rate in the distant versus near future (Mnear future = $12.44, SD = $10.63; Mdstant future = $11.41, SD = $8.14; F(1, 463) = 1.53, p = 0.22, Cohen’s d = .029). Additionally, there was no significant two-way interaction between procedure and timing (F(1, 463) = 0.139, p = 0.71; MTEL-Near Future = $15.71, SD = $10.68; MMEL-Near Future = $9.05, SD = $9.49; MTEL-Distant Future = 14.43, SD =8.27; MMEL-distant future = 8.38, SD = 6.80).(Figure 2).
targets.outcome_reasoning: The consecutive paragraph confirms the original TEL versus MEL main effect, expressly contrasts the absent timing main effect, and reports no procedure-by-timing interaction. Full title and author initials unavailable.

targets.authors: Plantinga, A.; Krijnen, J. M.; Zeelenberg, M.; Breugelmans, S. M.
targets.title: Evidence for opportunity cost neglect in the poor.
targets.evidence_quote: Plantinga, A., Krijnen, J. M., Zeelenberg, M., & Breugelmans, S. M. (2018). Evidence for opportunity cost neglect in the poor. Journal of Behavioral Decision Making, 31(1), 65-73.
targets.outcome_quote: The interaction was not reliable (OR: 1.02, z = 49, 95% CI [0.94, 1.11]), nor was the effect of income (OR: 1.01, z = .25, 95% CI [0.95, 1.07]).
targets.outcome_reasoning: Original central interaction is null in primary spreadsheet (r=-0.03, 95% CI [-0.11133135,0.04324818]); replication interaction is also null. Agreement is successful even without significance. Lower confidence because the narrative does not explicitly compare its null with the original null and project date labels disagree; full citation in write-up says 2018, summary says 2019.

targets.authors: Roux; Goldsmith; Bonezzi
targets.title: On the Psychology of Scarcity
targets.evidence_quote: We sought to replicate the findings of On the Psychology of Scarcity: Experiment 4 (Roux, Goldsmith, and Bonezzi, 2015).
targets.outcome_quote: This replication failed to find either a main effect (M  = $1.78, SD  = 1.20; F (1, 420) = 0.89, p  = .34; ηp2 = .00) or an interaction with SVO (β = .02, SE = .04, t(418) = 0.49, p = .62; ηp2 = .00).
targets.outcome_reasoning: Only the displayed short title and surnames are available in the acquired project report; no subtitle or initials inferred.

targets.authors: Shah; Zhao; Mullainathan; Shafir
targets.evidence_quote: Shah et al., 2018 Study 3 Replication
targets.outcome_quote: When asked to not think about how much they spend on driving, lower-income participants reported no more intrusions (7.62 [6.56, 8.69]) than did higher-income participants (7.19 [6.22, 8.15]), t(654) = 0.59, p = .55; interaction between income and condition F(1, 1330) = 1.00, p = .32, partial eta-squared(np2) = .001.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Primary hypothesis and original positive interaction are stated in the project files/spreadsheet; corresponding replication does not support it. Full title and author initials unavailable.

targets.authors: Shah, A. K.; Shafir, E.; Mullainathan, S.
targets.title: Scarcity frames value
targets.evidence_quote: The study attempted to replicate a previous finding by Shah, Shafir,  & Mullainathan (2015; Study 6 on Time Scarcity).
targets.outcome_quote: Contrary to prior results (Shah et el., 2015), there was no significant interaction between time-scarcity and account manipulation.

targets.authors: Tully, S. M.; Hershfield, H. E.; Meyvis, T.
targets.title: Seeking lasting enjoyment with limited money: Financial constraints increase preference for material goods over experiences
targets.evidence_quote: Tully, Hershfield & Meyvis (2015), Study 5
targets.outcome_quote: Although most of our replications did not approach statistical significance, those that did (4, 16–18) shared some common features.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Reference 18 is in the named successful set.

targets.authors: Zhu; Ratner
targets.title: Scarcity Polarizes Preferences: The Impact on Choice Among Multiple Items in a Product Class
targets.evidence_quote: Replication Attempt of Zhu & Ratner, 2015, Scarcity Polarizes Preferences: The Impact on Choice Among Multiple Items in a Product Class, Study 2
targets.outcome_quote: Results suggested that there was no significant difference between the scarce (M = 0.48, SD = 0.22) and abundant (M = 0.50, SD = 0.24) conditions on the proportion of favourites chosen, ZMann-Whitney = 1.04, p = 0.30.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Original greater favorite liking and choice share are described explicitly; both corresponding replication comparisons fail. Initials absent in the acquired text.

reasoning: Verified title, DOI and author boundaries against Europe PMC JATS. Cached parent text was inspected first but lacked provenance and omitted target-level details; acquired the full primary article and public primary OSF project reports, table, spreadsheet, and selected preregistrations. These are project-authored sources, not audit coder outputs. Coded 20 distinct original papers independently; Camerer is the closest target in its replication chain, not an added Shah (2012) target. Missing SI reference list prevented recovery of some full citations; retained only fields actually printed in acquired text. No external-memory DOIs supplied. Outcome comparisons use each target separately, including original null findings. No reproduction axes apply.
